decision_ownership: Historical research was organized by Codex/operator, not demonstrated autonomous LLM discovery.
startup_process: Early research could not qualify its unloaded baseline. It changed methods to separate static equilibrium/KKT and independent unloaded dynamics; task displacement could not yet be compared.

Small drift still coexisted with force-residual spikes. Active sets, integration steps and actual dynamic response helped separate numerical failure from physical explanations; apparent rest was insufficient.
Excellent local Jacobian row matching still failed under finite loading as tendons slackened. Research moved from local geometry to nonlinear equilibrium and loaded response.

Constraint geometry and route distribution became research variables. Abstract dense guide paths needed a separate check against actual solid guide holes; installed layouts changed several physical factors, so no unique causal attribution followed.
Good finite displacement could still fail tail-window residuals and settling. Physical material response was investigated in an explicitly authorized domain, without relaxing dynamic acceptance.

Promising installed designs required all conditions, independent replay and bounded numerical robustness checks. The result was a limited development numerical witness, not formal SELECT, global stability or hardware proof.
general_lessons: Before a qualified working point exists, distinguish failure to solve from structural infeasibility.
Unilateral lengths require actual taut/slack sets, multiplier signs and complementarity.
Local Jacobian matching cannot guarantee finite-load response.
When local parameter changes cease to add information, consider a different mathematical method, parameter group or physical mechanism.
Prefer experiments that distinguish competing explanations.
Static qualification, complete dynamics and independent acceptance are different evidence levels.
A low-value local route does not exhaust the legal research space.

trace.problem: The early campaign exhausted its allowance without a qualified unloaded baseline.
trace.interpretation: Loaded displacement from that initial state would not establish task performance.
trace.method_change: A separately authorized campaign investigated static equilibrium, KKT and independent unloaded dynamics.
trace.new_evidence: Qualified equilibria were established in that campaign.
trace.limit: The earlier failure and all costs remained; static qualification did not establish loaded success.

trace.problem: Small drift coexisted with force-residual spikes.
trace.interpretation: Apparent rest did not distinguish numerical effects from actual force imbalance.
trace.method_change: Compare unilateral active sets, time steps, force residuals and actual dynamic responses.
trace.new_evidence: Finer stepping yielded valid responses, but that finite campaign still had no performance witness.
trace.limit: This did not identify a unique failure cause or prove a mechanism impossible; current frozen integration settings remain authoritative.

trace.problem: Excellent local row-space matching failed finite-force dynamics.
trace.interpretation: Finite bending can shorten straight chords, slacken cables or violate route validity.
trace.method_change: Compare ideal kinematics, nonlinear hard-cable equilibrium and real soft-limit loaded dynamics.
trace.new_evidence: The comparison exposed finite-deformation effects absent from the local Jacobian.
trace.limit: A local match was a hypothesis screen, not a finite-load certificate.

trace.problem: Local parameter adjustments did not resolve finite-response limitations.
trace.interpretation: Constraint geometry and distribution of tendon paths could matter beyond material tuning.
trace.method_change: Investigate different route distributions and dense physical guiding ideas.
trace.new_evidence: Dense routes improved response in the historical campaign.
trace.limit: Those abstract routes were not yet the final installed design; improvement did not establish an implementable assembly.

trace.problem: Abstract guiding points differed from actual solid plate holes.
trace.interpretation: An ideal path cannot automatically be installed in a real assembly.
trace.method_change: Compare actual guide-hole layouts, routes and finite deformation.
trace.new_evidence: Physical layouts improved performance while masses and gaps also changed.
trace.limit: No single-factor segment-count explanation was established.

trace.problem: Favorable displacement still coexisted with tail residual or incomplete settling.
trace.interpretation: Finite-horizon material relaxation and dynamic balance remained separate obstacles.
trace.method_change: Investigate physical bending viscosity/material response within an explicitly versioned domain.
trace.new_evidence: Subsequent designs were assessed using actual tail-window residuals and speeds, not just instantaneous displacement.
trace.limit: The material was not experimentally calibrated; several design factors changed and no unique success cause was proved.

trace.problem: A promising search result alone did not establish reproducibility.
trace.interpretation: Search, unseen conditions and independent numerical checks serve different evidentiary roles.
trace.method_change: Freeze the promising design and run complete conditions, independent replay, refined stepping and initial perturbations.
trace.new_evidence: All historical conditions passed those bounded development checks without relaxing thresholds.
trace.limit: This historical numerical witness is context only, not this Study's evidence, formal SELECT, general stability or hardware proof.

scope: Answer-isolated research process. Exact winning geometry, payouts, material combinations, labels, raw references and reconstruction locations are omitted. Current model facts and authorization prevail; Main independently chooses whether any method transfers.
